items.en: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine
items.zh: 俄軍逾 400 架無人機與 110 枚飛彈襲烏，基輔至少 7 死
items.summary: Russia launched more than 400 drones and 110 missiles across Ukraine overnight, killing at least seven people in Kyiv, Al Jazeera reported. The scale of the barrage places it among the heaviest single nights of the war, striking the capital while air defences were stretched across several regions at once. The attack lands while US-led peace efforts remain unsettled, and it follows a pattern of mass strikes timed to periods of diplomatic pressure. Ukrainian officials were still assessing damage to residential buildings and energy infrastructure as rescue work continued through the day.

items.en: Russian strike kills two, wounds 60, in Zelenskyy's hometown
items.zh: 克里維里赫遭襲 2 死 60 傷，俄飛彈落入波蘭境內
items.summary: A Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's hometown, killed two people and wounded about 60, Al Jazeera reported. The attack came as Russian missiles landed inside NATO member Poland, raising the prospect of alliance consultations, and while US-led peace efforts face continuing uncertainty. Kryvyi Rih is an industrial city in central Ukraine that has been hit repeatedly, and the high casualty count reflects strikes falling in built-up residential areas. The spillover into Polish territory is the detail most likely to drive the diplomatic response this week.

items.en: Trump says he wants 'permanent' deal to stop Iran getting nuclear weapons
items.zh: 川普表態要與伊朗達成「永久性」禁核協議
items.summary: US President Donald Trump said he wants a permanent agreement preventing Iran from developing nuclear weapons, Al Jazeera reported. The remark arrives alongside a separate Al Jazeera analysis asking whether Tehran could reverse its stated civil-only nuclear policy, and against the backdrop of a US blockade of Iranian ports whose economic effect is still being assessed. Framing the goal as permanent rather than time-limited marks a departure from the expiring restrictions of the earlier nuclear accord, and it sets a high bar that Iranian officials have so far shown no sign of accepting.

items.en: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz as Iran tightens grip on shipping
items.zh: 荷姆茲海峽兩油輪受損，伊朗稱船隻觸及水雷
items.summary: A British maritime agency reported two incidents involving tankers near Oman, while Iran said one vessel caught fire after striking a naval mine, Al Jazeera reported. The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil, so damage to shipping there feeds directly into insurance premiums and freight rates. Al Jazeera separately reported that a US maritime agency had warned the Iranian blockade was already adding to rising Gulf risk premiums. For Taiwan, which imports nearly all of its crude, the route matters more than the headline suggests.

items.en: Thousands protest across Europe over living costs and housing
items.zh: 歐洲多國民眾上街抗議生活成本與住房問題
items.summary: Demonstrations in France and Portugal drew thousands of people protesting against the cost of living and housing shortages, Al Jazeera reported. The marches follow youth-led protests over education policy and economic hardship in several European countries, suggesting a broadening movement rather than isolated national disputes. Housing costs have become the sharpest expression of a wider affordability squeeze, with rents outpacing wages in major cities across the continent. Organisers in both countries have signalled further action, and governments facing tight budgets have limited room to respond with direct subsidies.

items.en: Riemann hypothesis: Has the world's most famous maths problem been cracked?
items.zh: 黎曼猜想疑被攻克，證明過程借助 Claude 完成
items.summary: Mathematicians say a claimed proof of the Riemann hypothesis, produced with the help of Claude, could be historic, but it may take weeks to verify, Al Jazeera reported. The hypothesis concerns the distribution of prime numbers and has resisted proof since 1859, making it one of the Clay Institute's Millennium Prize problems. The notable part is methodological: a large language model contributing to a frontier proof shifts the debate about where AI sits in mathematical research. Verification is the whole story here, and until specialists finish reading the argument the result stays provisional.

items.en: FBI national crime database suffers suspected breach: Reports
items.zh: FBI 全國犯罪資料庫疑遭入侵
items.summary: The FBI's national crime database is reported to have suffered a suspected breach, the latest in a string of hacks and outages affecting US government systems, Al Jazeera reported. The database underpins background checks and law-enforcement queries nationwide, so any compromise raises questions about both data confidentiality and the integrity of records relied on in court. Al Jazeera separately reported that Washington has appointed a new cybersecurity chief after a run of technology failures. No attribution has been confirmed, and the scope of any data accessed remains unclear.

items.en: US appoints new cybersecurity chief after series of tech failures
items.zh: 美國接連技術事故後任命新網路安全主管
items.summary: The United States has appointed a new cybersecurity chief following a series of technology failures, Al Jazeera reported. The change comes after repeated outages and breaches across federal systems, a pattern that has drawn congressional attention to how agencies procure and maintain critical infrastructure. Replacing the official in charge is the conventional first move, but the harder problem is structural: federal cyber defence spans many agencies with overlapping mandates and uneven budgets. Whether the new appointment carries authority across those boundaries will determine if anything changes in practice.

items.en: Chelsea beaten 4-1 by Leeds to suffer third loss in four in Premier League
items.zh: 切爾西主場 1:4 不敵里茲，近四場三敗
items.summary: Leeds United came from a goal down at Stamford Bridge to beat Chelsea 4-1, climbing above their hosts to sixth in the Premier League, Al Jazeera reported. It is Chelsea's third defeat in four league matches, a run that has turned a promising start into a question about squad depth and defensive organisation. For Leeds, taking four goals away from Stamford Bridge after conceding first is the kind of result that reframes a season. The table now has both clubs separated by a single place in the European chase.

items.en: Noni Madueke salvages draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United as Raya injured
items.zh: 馬杜埃克救回一分，阿森納客場平紐卡索、拉亞受傷
items.summary: Noni Madueke rescued a draw for Arsenal at Newcastle United, with goalkeeper David Raya picking up an injury during the match, Al Jazeera reported. League leaders Arsenal missed the chance to go eight points clear of second-placed Brighton, who play on Sunday, so the dropped points could matter by the end of the weekend. St James' Park has been a difficult trip for title contenders, and taking a point from a losing position is a defensible outcome. The Raya injury is the more consequential detail for the weeks ahead.

items.en: Liverpool vs Manchester United: Premier League - teams, prediction, lineups
items.zh: 利物浦主場迎戰曼聯，紅魔仍陷降級區
items.summary: One of football's biggest rivalries takes centre stage as Liverpool host a Manchester United side sitting in the Premier League relegation zone, Al Jazeera reported in its match preview with team news, predicted lineups and tactical notes. United arriving at Anfield in the bottom three is an unusual framing for this fixture, and it shifts the pressure entirely onto the visitors. For Liverpool the match is about converting home advantage into points in a congested top half. Kick-off falls on Sunday, so the result closes out the weekend's league programme.

items.en: South Korea cheating scandal: Are AI smart glasses a threat to exams?
items.zh: 韓國作弊案引爆討論：AI 智慧眼鏡是否威脅考試公平
items.summary: Al Jazeera examined whether AI-equipped smart glasses undermine exam integrity, after a cheating scandal in South Korea where the device sits at the centre of the case. South Korea's university entrance exam is unusually high-stakes, which makes it a stress test for invigilation rules written before wearable AI existed. The explainer notes that detection is the hard part: glasses look ordinary, and banning a category of eyewear outright creates its own problems. The question matters wherever closed-book exams still carry heavy weight, including Taiwan's own university assessments.

items.en: Police charge crowds at Brussels student march
items.zh: 布魯塞爾學生遊行遭警方驅散，抗議學費與教改
items.summary: Thousands of students and teachers marched in Brussels against higher tuition fees, education reforms and budget cuts, and police charged the crowds, Al Jazeera reported. The protest belongs to a wider wave of youth-led education demonstrations across Europe this autumn, including continuing actions in French suburbs where students say they have seen no change. Tuition increases and staffing cuts are the common thread, driven by governments consolidating budgets. The use of force against a student march raises a second argument about policing of protest alongside the education dispute itself.

items.en: Chinese student enrollment at Taiwanese universities falls to 34
items.zh: 中國學生在台攻讀學位人數降至 34 人
items.summary: The number of Chinese students enrolled in degree programmes at Taiwanese universities has dropped to 34, according to new data reported by Focus Taiwan, more than six years after Beijing suspended new applications during the COVID-19 pandemic. The figure marks the near-complete end of a cross-strait student flow that once numbered in the thousands and supported enrolment at private institutions. With Taiwan's own birth cohorts shrinking, universities have been redirecting recruitment toward Southeast Asia. The data point is small in absolute terms but tells a clear story about where cross-strait academic exchange now stands.

items.en: US tech sell-off continues as Anthropic tumbles after mega IPO
items.zh: Anthropic 掛牌後重挫，美科技股賣壓延續
items.summary: Anthropic's shares fell sharply in the days after its record listing, extending the US technology sell-off, Al Jazeera reported; the IPO had been viewed as a potential boost for an industry struggling to regain its footing. Anthropic raised 81.3 billion dollars at a 1.5 trillion dollar valuation, pricing shares at 83 dollars in the largest initial public offering ever, surpassing SpaceX. The debut failing to steady sentiment is the signal investors took from the week, and Asian markets fell alongside Wall Street as AI-bubble worries deepened.

items.en: Trump threatens tax on US tech firms building AI data centres abroad
items.zh: 川普揚言對海外建 AI 資料中心的美企課重稅
items.summary: US President Donald Trump warned that American technology companies will face what he called a tremendous tax if they build AI data centres abroad, Al Jazeera reported. Data-centre siting is driven by power availability, cooling and land, which is why operators have been looking outside the United States as domestic grid constraints bite. A tax on foreign build-out would push capital expenditure back home at exactly the moment utilities are warning about load growth. For Asian suppliers of servers, power equipment and cooling, the location of the next build cycle is the whole question.

items.en: US signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months
items.zh: 美半年內核准近 90 萬顆 AI 晶片輸中
items.summary: A US House committee released export data showing Washington approved sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China over six months, Al Jazeera reported, published amid scrutiny of a former Nvidia chief executive's alleged links to a Chinese spy. The volume is large enough to complicate the official account of how tightly advanced accelerators are controlled. Export licensing has become the main lever in US-China technology policy, and disclosure of the actual approval numbers gives Congress a concrete basis to argue the controls are looser than advertised.

items.en: Ado announces 'Ado no Utattemita Tour 2027', six shows in three cities
items.zh: Ado 公布「歌ってみたツアー2027」，三城六場、1/10 開跑
items.summary: Ado has announced Ado no Utattemita Tour 2027, six shows across three cities beginning on 10 January to mark her tenth anniversary as a singer, Skream! reported. The tour is built around her cover-song work rather than original material, and a cover album is set for release at the end of this year. Earliest ballot access runs through her fan club, which opened member pre-sales first. No overseas leg has been announced, so Taiwan fans tracking this one should watch for a later Asia addition.

items.en: Official HIGE DANdism set first Asia tour in two years, including Taipei
items.zh: Official髭男dism 兩年來首度亞洲巡演，台北為四城之一
items.summary: Official HIGE DANdism have confirmed their first Asia tour in about two years, six shows across four cities covering Seoul, Taipei, Singapore and Bangkok, Japanese music outlet Natalie reported. The Taipei date is the one that matters locally, and the band also ran a pop-up store in Taipei timed to the tour. Fan-club pre-sale registration opened through Ticket Plus. The band last played Taipei Arena and told local press they wanted to return quickly, so the Taipei booking has been among the more anticipated Japanese shows of the cycle.

items.en: Aimer announces national hall tour starting next September
items.zh: Aimer 宣布明年 9 月起全國 Hall 巡演
items.summary: Aimer has announced a national hall tour in Japan beginning next September, Skream! reported. Hall-sized rooms suit her material better than arenas and typically mean a longer run of dates with better sightlines, which is how her previous tours have been configured. The announcement is early enough that the full schedule and ticketing details will follow in stages. For listeners in Taiwan, the relevant pattern is that her overseas appearances have come as festival slots or one-off shows rather than as legs attached to a domestic hall tour.

items.en: back number to hold 2027 fan club tour across livehouses, halls and arenas
items.zh: back number 2027 年粉絲俱樂部巡演，跨 Live House 到大型場館
items.summary: back number will stage a 2027 fan club tour running across livehouses, halls and arenas, Billboard Japan reported. Mixing venue sizes in a single run is unusual and effectively creates two different shows, with the small rooms being the hard tickets. Access is through the fan club, so membership rather than general sale decides who gets in. The band has also been running its one room party series alongside regular touring. No Asian dates are attached, which is consistent with how their fan-club runs have been kept domestic.
